main_text.p: &tenacius hæreant. Et quoniā verba sunt πτερόεντα[?], hoc est alata, quæ quasi volant irreuocabilia,& nisi literis mandentur, ad posteros & absentes perferri nequeunt: Christus consulturus nostræ ruditati memoriam fui corporis & sanguinis,quò durabilior foret,in visibilibus signis, pani & vino quodammodo alligare voluit. Adde quòd vehementius mouent quę in oculos quàm quæ in aures incurrunt. Quantum C. Cęsaris interfecti vestimenta cruenta à M. Antonio in cōcione prolata, potuerint ad populum Romanum in tyrannicidas concitandum, historiæ testantur. Quantum pondus vaticiniis Ieremiæ attulit baltheus ille lumbaris ad Euphratem in foramine petræ abscōditus? Item fidelia à figulo coëmpta, & in oculis virorum confracta? Item lora & iuga collo Prophetæ accommodata? Quibus verba Prophetæ, res illas visibiles explicantia, postquā fuerunt adiecta, populus Iudaicus inde

page.notes: The Greek word after "verba sunt" is blurred; read as πτερόεντα with doubt, marked [?]. The paragraph division inside the text is unclear from indentation, so the page is treated as one paragraph. The faint mirrored letters at the left edge are show-through and were left out. The page number is read as 41 from the printed "4" and superscript-looking "1".
